title: Why Automatic Saving Beats Willpower

beats.say: You save more when it is automatic: eighty six percent joined, compared with about twenty.
beats.visual: a single open door at the end of a quiet hallway with warm light, no people

beats.say: Economists Brigitte Madrian and Dennis Shea studied one large company that switched to automatic enrollment.
beats.visual: an old filing cabinet with one drawer pulled open in soft window light, no people

beats.say: The switch happened in nineteen ninety eight, and it applied to new hires.
beats.visual: a paper calendar page turning on a wooden desk, macro, no people

beats.say: Among workers hired under automatic enrollment, eighty six percent joined the retirement plan.
beats.visual: a full glass jar of coins glowing on a dark shelf, warm light, no people

beats.say: Under the old opt in rule, only about twenty percent had joined after three months.
beats.visual: a mostly empty glass jar with a few coins at the bottom, soft light, no people

beats.say: The plan was the same. Only the default changed.
beats.visual: two identical doors side by side, one open and one closed, soft hallway light

beats.say: That is the default effect: people tend to stay with whatever is chosen for them.
beats.visual: a river flowing along a worn stone channel at dawn, wide shot, no people

beats.say: Here is the part nobody tells you. Many workers also kept the default contribution and fund.
beats.visual: a long winding road stretching to a distant horizon in morning mist, no people

beats.say: The honest catch: a default is not always right for you. The starting rate may be too low.
beats.visual: a stormy sea with waves rising under a heavy sky and a lighthouse in the distance, no people

beats.say: You can check your own plan and change your rate if it does not fit.
beats.visual: a hand turning a small brass dial on an old machine, close-up, no faces

beats.say: One simple move is to set up the saving to happen automatically yourself.
beats.visual: a calendar with one repeating date circled in soft light, no people

beats.say: This is education, not advice. Make the good choice the easy choice.
beats.visual: a quiet kitchen table at morning with a coffee cup and a notepad, no people

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: an empty highway stretching toward a glowing sunrise horizon, wide shot, no people

description: In a classic study of one large company, automatic 401(k) enrollment lifted participation among new hires to 86 percent, versus about 20 percent after three months under the old opt-in rule. Defaults shape behavior. A default may not fit you. Educational only, not financial advice.
first_comment: Is your saving automatic or do you have to remember? Educational only, not financial advice.

facts.claim: At one Fortune 500 company that adopted automatic 401(k) enrollment on 1998-04-01, new hires had an 86% participation rate; under opt-in only about 20% participated after three months (65% after 36 months)
facts.basis: Madrian and Shea (2001), The Power of Suggestion, Quarterly Journal of Economics 116(4); NBER w7682

facts.claim: A substantial fraction of auto-enrolled workers kept the default contribution rate and fund allocation
Results come from one company; other firms and plans differ

caption: At one big company, automatic enrollment got 86% of new hires into the 401(k), versus about 20% after three months with opt-in. Same plan, different default. A default may not fit you. Educational content, not financial advice.
